cues.en: Hello, Internet. Thoughts compete for space in your brain. Cat photos, news stories, belief structures, funny GIFs, educational videos, not so educational videos, and your thinking inventory is limited. A thought without a brain to think it dies. Now we can treat thoughts as though they're alive, specifically alive like germs. That might sound weird, but stick with me. Take jokes. Jokes are thought germs that live in your brain. And when you tell the joke to another brain, you help it to reproduce.
cues.zh: 大家好，互联网的朋友们。各种想法都在争夺你大脑里的空间。猫咪照片、新闻故事、信仰体系、搞笑 GIF、科普视频、不那么科普的视频，而你的思考容量是有限的。没有大脑去思考的想法就会消亡。现在我们可以把思想看作是有生命的，确切地说，像病菌一样有生命。听起来可能有点怪，但先听我说完。比如笑话。笑话就是寄生在你大脑里的“思想病菌”。当你把笑话讲给另一个人听时，你就在帮它繁殖。

cues.en: Just like when you have the flu and sneeze to help it reproduce. This germ gets into its host by snot through the mouth and this one by words through the ear, but it's reproduction either way. Logging on to your social media then is exposing yourself to everyone's mental sneezes. Each post a glob of snot with a thought germ trying to get into your brain. If not for permanent residents, then at least long enough to get you to press the share button and sneeze it with everyone you know. In this analogy then, a funny cat photo with the perfect caption is a super flu. Now just as germs exploit weak points in your immune system, so do thought germs exploit weak points in your brain, aka emotions.
cues.zh: 就像你得了流感打喷嚏帮它繁殖一样。这种病菌通过鼻涕从嘴巴进入宿主，而另一种则通过话语从耳朵进入，但不管哪种方式都是在繁殖。所以，登录社交媒体就等于把自己暴露在所有人精神上的喷嚏之中。每条帖子都是一团带着思想病菌的鼻涕，想方设法钻进你的大脑。就算不能永久定居，至少也想待到你按下分享键，把它打喷嚏似地喷给所有你认识的人。照这个比喻，一张配上绝妙文案的搞笑猫咪照片，就是一场超级流感。正如生理病菌会利用你免疫系统的漏洞，思想病菌也会利用你大脑的弱点——也就是情绪。

cues.en: Once inside, thought germs that press emotional buttons get their host to spread them more, measurably more. Well, except sadness. Sad thoughts don't get very far. Awe is pretty good, which is why websites that construct thought germs like biological weapons arm them with titles like seven whatevers that will blow your mind or the shocking secret behind this thing. But anger is the ultimate edge for a thought germ. Anger bypasses your mental immune system and compels you to share it like nothing else. Being aware of your brain's weak spots is necessary for good mental health, like knowing how to wash your hands. Because even without intentional construction, any thought germ on the Internet can, on its own, grow more infectious as it spreads. To talk about why, let's forget anger for a moment and go back to that cat photo. Every photo ever taken is a thought germ, and most die a quick death like the bazillion cat photos or baby photos posted on the Internet that are never shared. But a mildly funny cat photo can grow into so much more because just as transatlantic
cues.zh: 一旦侵入，触动情绪开关的思想病菌就能促使宿主更广泛地传播它们，传播量会有肉眼可见的增加。呃，悲伤除外。悲伤的想法传不远。“惊叹”效果就很不错，所以那些像制造生化武器一样炮制思想病菌的网站，总会配上诸如“让你大开眼界的七大某某”，或者“某某背后的惊天秘密”之类的标题。但对于思想病菌来说，愤怒才是终极杀器。愤怒能绕过你的精神免疫系统，以前所未有的力量迫使你去分享。了解自己大脑的弱点对心理健康至关重要，就像懂得如何洗手一样。因为即使没有人故意制造，互联网上的任何思想病菌在传播过程中也会自行变得更具传染性。要解释原因，我们先别谈愤怒，回到刚才那张猫咪照片。拍下的每一张照片都是一个思想病菌，其中绝大多数都很快夭折，就像网上发了无数却无人转发的猫猫照或宝宝照一样。但一张略微搞笑的猫咪照片却能发展成气候，因为正如跨大西洋

cues.en: flights were the best thing to happen to germ germs, so the Internet is the best thing to happen to thought germs. For once on board, that cat photo can leap into other brains, and those brains might share it, and here's the key point, occasionally
cues.zh: 航班是真正病菌的最大福音一样，互联网也是思想病菌的最大福音。因为一旦登机，那张猫咪照片就能跳进其他人的大脑，那些大脑可能会分享它，而且——关键在于——偶尔还会

cues.en: change it. A Photoshop here, a tweaked caption there. Most changes are terrible, but some make the thought germ even funnier, getting more brains to share it, which results in more changes and a shot at superstardom.
cues.zh: 改造它。这里 P 一下图，那里改句文案。大多数改动都很烂，但有些改动会让这个思想病菌变得更搞笑，吸引更多大脑去分享，从而引发更多的二次创作，甚至有机会一炮走红。

cues.en: Thus, a lowly cat photo can achieve global brain domination,
cues.zh: 就这样，一张不起眼的猫咪照片就能席卷全球人类的大脑，

cues.en: at least for a few hours. The Internet, with its unparalleled ability to share and randomly change thought germs, can't help but make them stronger. With jokes, that's awesome. But with angry germs, not always so awesome. No. Angry germs, the more they're shared, undergo the same process, changing and distorting to be more aggravating.
cues.zh: 至少能占领几个小时。互联网拥有无与伦比的传播和随机构想思想病菌的能力，必然会使它们变得更强。对笑话来说，这很棒。但对愤怒病菌而言，就未必那么妙了。不，愤怒病菌在传播得越多时，也会经历同样的过程，不断演变、扭曲，变得更具煽动性。

cues.en: These have a better chance of spreading than their possibly more accurate, but probably also more boring rivals.
cues.zh: 比起那些可能更准确、但也可能更无趣的对手，它们往往更容易传播。

cues.en: But like plagues, thought germs can burn through a population too quickly. Just watch your favorite meme generating machine for a week, and you'll see the life cycle fly by. However, some thought germs have found a way around burnout. Now, I must warn you, depending on which thought germs live in your head and which you fight for, the next section might sound horrifying.
cues.zh: 但就像瘟疫一样，思想病菌在人群中消耗得太快。只要观察你最喜欢的梗图生成工具一周，就能看到一个生命周期飞速闪过。然而，有些思想病菌找到了避免自我消耗殆尽的方法。不过我必须提醒你，取决于你脑海中存活着哪种思想病菌、你又在为哪种而战，接下来这部分内容可能会听起来很惊悚。

cues.en: So please keep in mind, we're talking about what makes some thought germs successful,
cues.zh: 所以请记住，我们讨论的是什么让某些思想病菌取得成功，

cues.en: particularly angry ones, and not how good or how bad the thoughts themselves are. Deep breath, calm. Thought germs can burn out because once everyone agrees, it's hard to keep talking and thus thinking about them. But if there's an opposing thought germ, an argument, then the thinking never has to stop. The disagreement doesn't have to be angry, but, again, angry helps. The more visible an argument gets, the more bystanders it draws in, which makes it more visible, which is why every group from the most innocuous Internet forum to the national conversation can turn into a double rage storm across the sky in no time. Wait. These thought germs aren't competing,
cues.zh: 尤其是愤怒类的，而不是思想本身的优劣好坏。深呼吸，放轻松。思想病菌之所以会消亡，是因为一旦大家达成共识，就很难再继续讨论并思考它们。但如果存在一个对立的思想病菌、一场争论，那么思考就永远不必停下。争执不一定要充满愤怒，但愤怒确实大有助益。争论越受瞩目，吸引的旁观者就越多，从而变得更加瞩目，这就是为什么从最不起眼的网络论坛到全国性话题，任何圈子都能在转瞬之间演变成一场遮天蔽日的双向愤怒风暴。等等，这些思想病菌并没有在竞争，

cues.en: Working together, they reach more brains and hold their thoughts longer than they could alone. Thought germs on opposite sides of an argument can be symbiotic.
cues.zh: 通过协同合作，它们侵入的大脑更多，占据思维的时间也比单打独斗更长。争论对立面的思想病菌，其实可以形成共生关系。

cues.en: One tool symbiotic anger germs in particular can employ is you're with us or against us. Whatever thought germ does left to the front of your brain, push it back. This video isn't about that. We're just talking about this tool, which makes it very hard for neutral brains to resist, and its divisiveness
cues.zh: 共生愤怒病菌尤其会使用的一种工具，就是“非友即敌”。无论刚才是哪个思想病菌蹿到了你脑海前线，先把它压下去。本期视频不讨论具体立场，我们只探讨这个工具，它让保持中立的大脑极难抗拒，而且它的撕裂性

cues.en: also grows its symbiotic partner. This explains why in some arguments, gaining more allies also gains more enemies. Because though the participants think they're involved in a fiery battle to the death, from the anger germs perspective, one side is a field of flowers and the other a flock of butterflies.
cues.zh: 同样会滋养它的共生伙伴。这就解释了为什么在某些争论中，拉来更多盟友的同时也会引来更多敌人。因为尽管参与者认为自己卷入了一场誓死方休的激战，但在愤怒病菌看来，一方是一片花海，另一方则是一群蝴蝶。

cues.en: Of course, planting more flowers will get you more butterflies, and getting more butterflies will pollinate more flowers. If there is some argument that splits the population and lasts forever and that even the most neutral people find difficult to avoid, you just might be looking at a super successful pair of symbiotic anger germs that have reached ecological stability.
cues.zh: 当然，种出更多花朵会引来更多蝴蝶，而吸引更多蝴蝶又会为更多花朵授粉。如果有某种争论撕裂了人群且经久不息，连最中立的人都避无可避，那你看到的很可能就是一对超级成功、并已达到生态平衡的共生愤怒病菌。

cues.en: Now one final depressing thought. I mean, one more awe inspiring point that will reveal the secrets of... Actually, no. It's just depressing. When opposing groups get big, they don't really argue with each other. They mostly argue with themselves about how angry the other group makes them. We can actually graph fights on the Internet to see this in action. Each becomes its own quasi isolated Internet sharing thoughts about the other. You see where this is going. Right? Each group breeds thought germs about the other, and as before, the most enraging, but not necessarily the most accurate spread the fastest. The group almost can't help but construct a totem of the other so enraging. They'll talk about it all the time, which now that you know how thought germs grow is exactly what makes the totem always perfectly maddening. Now all this isn't to say there's no point in arguing. That's a different video. Or that the Internet isn't amazing or that there aren't things worth trying to change people's minds about. Thought germs of all kinds come and go. But it's useful to be aware of how thoughts can use our emotions to spread and how
cues.zh: 现在说最后一个令人沮丧的想法。我是说，还有一个令人惊叹、将揭示……秘密的观点。其实不。它就是令人沮丧。当对立群体变大时，他们并不会真的互相争论。他们主要是在跟自己争论：对方让自己有多生气。我们其实可以把互联网上的争吵画成图，看看它如何发生。每一方都变成自己近乎孤立的互联网，分享关于对方的想法。你知道这会走向哪里，对吧？每个群体都在滋生关于对方的思想病菌，而和之前一样，最让人愤怒、却不一定最准确的思想病菌传播得最快。这个群体会几乎忍不住把对方塑造成一个极其令人愤怒的图腾。他们会一直谈论它；而既然你知道思想病菌如何生长，就会明白这正是这个图腾总能完美激怒人的原因。这一切并不是说争论没有意义。那是另一个视频的内容。也不是说互联网不神奇，或者没有值得改变别人想法的事情。各种思想病菌来来去去。但意识到思想如何利用我们的情绪传播，以及思想能传播得有多

cues.en: rapidly a thought is able to spread, the more chances it has to become even better at spreading through random changes that are made to it. Sometimes that's great. Sometimes it's terrible. But if you want to maintain a healthy brain, it pays to be cautious of thoughts that have passed through a lot of other brains and that poke you where your weakest. It's your brain. Be hygienic with it.
cues.zh: 快：一种思想传播得越快，它通过随机变化变得更擅长传播的机会就越多。有时这很棒。有时很糟。但如果你想保持大脑健康，就要警惕那些经过许多其他大脑、并戳中你最脆弱之处的想法。这是你的大脑。保持大脑卫生。
